review_candidates.title: Sr Infrastructure Engineer
review_candidates.description: The Senior Infrastructure Engineer serves as the designated backup and knowledge-continuity resource for Baylor Genetics’ on-premises data center and network environment. This role exists to ensure uninterrupted operation of the critical infrastructure supporting our genomics pipeline and clinical laboratory systems, and to eliminate single points of failure in IT operations. This role may evolve as organizational needs change. Exists to sustain, document, and be fully capable of independently operating all core on-premises infrastructure — servers, storage, networking, and security systems — in any operational scenario, including emergency coverage of the primary infrastructure lead. Impacts clinical laboratory operations, genomics pipeline throughput, and the reliability of all on-premises and hybrid-connected systems used across the organization. Success looks like: zero unplanned outages attributable to single-person dependency, a fully documented environment with up-to-date runbooks, and the demonstrated ability to assume full infrastructure ownership without disruption. Key Responsibilities Serve as the designated backup for the primary infrastructure lead — assume full operational control of data center, network, and server environments during absences, emergencies, or transitions to ensure zero service interruption. Administer and maintain physical and virtual server infrastructure (Windows Server, Linux, VMware/Hyper-V), including provisioning, patching, performance monitoring, and capacity planning to sustain 99.9%+ uptime. Manage LAN/WAN networking operations including switches, routers, firewalls, and VLANs to maintain high availability and security across all on-premises systems. Build, maintain, and continuously improve runbooks, network diagrams, and disaster recovery documentation to eliminate single points of failure and reduce mean time to recovery. Support and sustain the on-premises genomics pipeline infrastructure, ensuring compute and storage resources meet demanding throughput and availability requirements for clinical laboratory operations. Collaborate cross-functionally with bioinformatics, clinical lab, and IT teams to align infrastructure reliability with patient-impacting laboratory workflows. Proactively identify and remediate risks including aging hardware, technical debt, and configuration vulnerabilities — presenting actionable proposals to leadership. Respond to infrastructure incidents and outages with urgency, including after-hours escalations, to minimize downtime impact on laboratory and clinical operations. Perform other duties as assigned to support team and organizational objectives. Comply with all company policies, procedures, and applicable regulatory requirements. Qualifications Required Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field; or equivalent technical training and experience. 7+ years of hands-on enterprise IT infrastructure engineering experience in a complex, predominantly on-premises environment. Deep expertise in physical and virtual server administration (Windows Server 2016/2019/2022, Linux) including VMware vSphere or Microsoft Hyper-V. Strong networking fundamentals: routing, switching, VLANs, firewall policy management, and systematic network troubleshooting (Cisco, Palo Alto, Fortinet, or equivalent). Experience managing physical data center environments — rack/stack, structured cabling, power, and cooling awareness. Proficiency with SAN/NAS storage platforms and enterprise backup/recovery systems (Veeam, Commvault, or equivalent). Working knowledge of Microsoft 365 and Azure Active Directory in a hybrid on-premises/cloud context. Strong documentation discipline: ability to produce clear runbooks, network diagrams, and standard operating procedures independently. Proven ability to rapidly learn complex, undocumented environments and operate independently under high-pressure conditions. Equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered. Preferred Experience in a healthcare, clinical laboratory, genomics, or other regulated life sciences environment. 7+ years of progressive experience in enterprise infrastructure roles with demonstrated ownership of critical systems. Relevant certifications: CCNA/CCNP, VCP-DCV, MCSE, CompTIA Network+/Security+, or equivalent. Familiarity with HPC or high-throughput bioinformatics pipeline infrastructure. Exposure to HIPAA compliance requirements, NIST frameworks, or SOC 2 audit environments. Scripting proficiency (PowerShell, Bash, or Python) for infrastructure automation and administrative efficiency. Experience with monitoring platforms such as PRTG, SolarWinds, Zabbix, or similar tools. COMPETENCIES Advanced systems and network troubleshooting — able to diagnose and resolve complex infrastructure issues across server, storage, and network layers independently. Infrastructure documentation and knowledge transfer — consistently produces clear, actionable runbooks and SOPs that allow others to execute without prior context. Operational resilience under pressure — calm, methodical decision-making during incidents and outages in environments where downtime directly impacts patient care. Cross-functional collaboration — effectively partners with bioinformatics, clinical lab, and IT teams to align infrastructure performance with organizational mission. Proactive risk identification — anticipates infrastructure vulnerabilities and aging hardware risks, and drives remediation before failures occur. PHYSICAL DEMANDS AND WORK ENVIRONMENT Location: Houston, TX. This position is a hybrid work environment. Most work can be done remotely but must have the ability to arrive on-site at our Houston Location in a reasonable amount of time if necessary. Must be able to lift and move equipment up to 50 lbs; perform physical tasks in a data center environment including rack/stack of servers and network hardware. Ability to work in environments with variable temperatures (data center cooling), moderate noise levels, and continuous standing or walking during data center operations. Occasional after-hours availability required for scheduled maintenance windows, incident response, and emergency infrastructure coverage. Must be authorized to work in the United States; visa sponsorship is not available for this position. No regular travel required; occasional travel to offsite data center or disaster recovery locations may arise. Baylor Genetics is proud to be an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse workplace. We welcome and encourage applicants from all backgrounds to apply. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, childbirth, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law. If you need an accommodation during the application process, please contact our Human Resources team. Note To Recruiters We value building direct relationships with our candidates and prefer to manage our hiring process internally. While we occasionally partner with select recruitment agencies for specialized roles, we do not accept unsolicited resumes from recruiters or agencies without a written agreement executed by the authorized signatory for Baylor Genetics ("Agreement"). Any resumes submitted to Baylor Genetics in the absence of an Agreement executed by Baylor Genetics' authorized signatory will be considered the property of Baylor Genetics, and Baylor Genetics will not be obligated to pay any associated recruitment fees.

review_candidates.description: Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms. Job Overview We are seeking a highly skilled and motivated Senior Systems Engineer to lead the design, deployment, and ongoing maintenance of our data center infrastructure. This position is critical to supporting our mission-critical systems and ensuring high availability, scalability, and performance across both on-premise and cloud environments. The ideal candidate will have deep technical expertise in both Windows and Linux environments, extensive experience with monitoring and disaster recovery solutions, and a strong foundation in virtualization, cloud services, storage, and preferably high-performance computing (HPC). This role requires a hands-on, detail-oriented engineer who thrives in a fast-paced, high-growth environment. Responsibilities Lead architecture, deployment, and lifecycle management of data center infrastructure components. Design and implement scalable, secure, and resilient systems in hybrid environments (on-prem and cloud). Administer and maintain enterprise Windows and Linux systems. Develop and enforce backup, disaster recovery, and business continuity strategies. Optimize storage and compute infrastructure for high performance and cost-effectiveness. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to support application needs and integration projects. Document systems designs, procedures, configurations, and provide knowledge transfer. Proactively monitor systems performance and reliability, and troubleshoot issues as they arise. Ensure compliance with industry standards and internal security policies. Participate in an on-call rotation and respond to incidents with urgency and professionalism. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Systems, Engineering, or related field (or equivalent experience). 7+ years of experience in systems engineering or infrastructure roles. Proficiency in both Windows Server and Linux (RHEL/CentOS/Ubuntu) environments. Proven experience in data center design, build-out, and operations. Strong knowledge of backup and disaster recovery solutions (e.g., Veeam, Commvault, Rubrik). Experience with cloud platforms such as AWS/AWS GovCloud, Azure, or GCP. Familiarity with enterprise storage solutions (e.g., NetApp, Dell EMC, Ceph). Experience with virtualization technologies (e.g., VMware, Hyper-V). Strong scripting and automation skills (e.g., PowerShell, Bash, Python). Understanding of networking fundamentals and integration with infrastructure systems. Excellent problem-solving skills, with the ability to multitask and work under pressure. Physical Demands: Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer Occasional standing and walking within the office Manual dexterity to operate a computer keyboard, mouse, and other office equipment Visual acuity to read screens, documents, and reports Occasional reaching, bending, or stooping to access file drawers, cabinets, or office supplies Lifting and carrying items up to 20 pounds occasionally (e.g., office supplies, packages) Benefits: Medical Insurance: Comprehensive health insurance plans covering a range of services Saronic pays 100% of the premium for employees and 80% for dependents Dental and Vision Insurance: Coverage for routine dental check-ups, orthodontics, and vision care Saronic pays 100% of the premium under the basic plan for employees and 80% for dependents Time Off: Generous PTO and Holidays Parental Leave: Paid maternity and paternity leave to support new parents Competitive Salary: Industry-standard salaries with opportunities for performance-based bonuses Retirement Plan: 401(k) plan with company match Stock Options: Equity options to give employees a stake in the company’s success Life and Disability Insurance: Basic life insurance and short- and long-term disability coverage Pet Insurance: Discounted pet insurance options including 24/7 Telehealth helpline Additional Perks: Free lunch benefit and unlimited free drinks and snacks in the office Saronic CCPA Notice for Candidates and California Employees If this role is based in the United States, it requires access to export-controlled information or items that require “U.S. Person” status. Saronic does not discriminate on the basis of race, sex, color, religion, age, national origin, marital status, disability, veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity or any other reason prohibited by law in provision of employment opportunities and benefits. We are also committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities.

review_candidates.description: About NCR VOYIX NCR Voyix Corporation (NYSE: VYX) is a global platform-powered leader in unified commerce for shopping and dining. Combining a flexible, intelligent platform with end-to-end payments capabilities and services developed through its deep industry experience, NCR Voyix empowers retailers and restaurants to accelerate new possibilities for their operations, experiences and business outcomes. NCR Voyix is headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, and serves customers in more than 35 countries worldwide. Manager, Network Engineering Onsite Position: Atlanta, GA Position Summary NCR Voyix is seeking a hands-on Manager, Network Engineering to lead our global network engineering team while remaining deeply involved in the design, implementation, and operation of our enterprise data center and core network infrastructure. This is a true player-coach role, ideal for a technical leader who enjoys mentoring engineers while continuing to work directly on complex networking initiatives. You will be responsible for leading a globally distributed team of network engineers, driving operational excellence, and providing technical leadership across Cisco ACI, Nexus infrastructure, data center interconnects, routing, and enterprise network modernization initiatives. The ideal candidate combines strong people leadership skills with deep technical expertise and can confidently guide architectural decisions, review production configurations, resolve critical incidents, and ensure engineering teams are delivering secure, scalable, and highly available network solutions. Key Responsibilities Technical Leadership & Player-Coach Responsibilities Serve as the senior technical leader and escalation point for complex networking issues across the enterprise. Maintain a hands-on role in the design, review, implementation, and support of enterprise network solutions. Participate directly in architecture reviews, configuration validation, change management activities, and major production deployments. Lead troubleshooting efforts and root-cause analysis for high-impact incidents affecting critical business services. Ensure engineering teams are following established standards, operational procedures, and best practices. Partner with architects and infrastructure teams to align network strategy with business objectives. Mentor engineers through technical challenges and support their professional growth and development. People Leadership & Global Team Management Lead and manage a globally distributed team of approximately six network engineers across multiple regions and time zones. Provide day-to-day coaching, technical guidance, performance feedback, and career development support. Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, continuous improvement, and technical excellence. Balance operational support requirements with strategic infrastructure initiatives. Establish and maintain engineering documentation, standards, processes, and operational runbooks. Support workforce planning, skills development, and team growth initiatives. Data Center & Core Network Engineering Lead the design, implementation, and operation of Cisco ACI-based data center environments. Manage and optimize Cisco APIC policies, tenants, endpoint groups (EPGs), contracts, and lifecycle upgrades. Oversee Cisco Nexus switching infrastructure supporting data center and enterprise networking environments. Design and support data center interconnect (DCI) solutions that ensure resiliency, performance, and business continuity. Provide technical leadership for core routing, switching, and network transport services. Ensure network designs support scalability, high availability, and future growth requirements. Routing & Edge Connectivity Own enterprise routing standards and strategy leveraging BGP and OSPF. Lead the design and operation of edge routing environments supporting enterprise, cloud, and external connectivity. Support Nexus-based routing and switching platforms across data center and edge environments. Drive network resiliency initiatives and optimization efforts to improve service availability and performance. Infrastructure Modernization & Operational Excellence Lead initiatives focused on network modernization, resiliency, automation, and operational efficiency. Partner with cloud, security, and infrastructure teams on hybrid networking projects and connectivity solutions. Evaluate emerging technologies and recommend improvements to network architecture and operational processes. Drive continuous improvements in monitoring, observability, incident response, and service reliability. Required Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. 8+ years of hands-on experience in enterprise networking, data center infrastructure, or network engineering. 2+ years of experience leading, mentoring, or managing network engineering teams. Strong hands-on expertise with: Cisco ACI Cisco Nexus (NX-OS) BGP and OSPF routing Data center networking and switching Data Center Interconnect (DCI) architectures Enterprise routing and switching platforms Proven ability to balance technical execution with people leadership responsibilities. Experience working directly with production configurations, change management processes, and troubleshooting complex network environments. Strong communication and stakeholder management skills. Preferred Qualifications Experience supporting large-scale, global, or mission-critical network environments. Previous experience serving as a technical lead, senior engineer, or escalation resource. Experience with hybrid cloud networking and cloud connectivity architectures. Knowledge of network automation, infrastructure as code, and network observability platforms. Experience leading infrastructure modernization and resiliency initiatives. Cisco certifications such as CCNP, CCIE, Data Center, Enterprise Infrastructure, or equivalent experience. Experience managing distributed teams across multiple geographic regions. Why Join NCR Voyix? This is a unique opportunity to lead a global network engineering team while remaining deeply involved in the technology. You'll influence the future of NCR Voyix's data center and core network infrastructure, mentor a talented team of engineers, and drive modernization initiatives that support critical business operations around the world. If you're a hands-on technical leader who thrives in a player-coach environment, we'd love to hear from you. review_candidates.title: Economic Empowerment Program Manager
review_candidates.description: The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future. Job Overview The Economic Empowerment Program Manager will build a workforce development program for IRC Montana from the ground up — designing service delivery, establishing employer and community partnerships, and expanding the program into new geographic areas across the state. This role combines program design, direct relationship-building, and public-sector engagement, with a particular focus on establishing IRC Montana's presence within local workforce development boards as a sustainable, long-term funding and partnership strategy. Helena is a strategic priority for this role, given its location as the seat of Montana's workforce development board and several key donors — offering an early opportunity to establish IRC's presence and build a lasting network there. Key Responsibilities Program Development Design and launch a workforce development program from the ground up — including service design, eligibility criteria, intake and referral processes, case management, and success metrics. Develop program policies, procedures, and client-facing materials suited to Montana's rural and geographically dispersed population. Conduct outreach and recruitment of prospective participants, screening and assessing for program eligibility. Collaborate with the development team on new program design and grant proposals to grow services; contribute to program and office-wide strategic planning, with measurable goals for placements, partnerships, and reach. Workforce Development Board Engagement Identify and regularly attend the workforce development board(s) covering each Montana community IRC serves, securing access through partner relationships where meetings are not readily public. Position IRC Montana as the local expert on serving English Language Learners and diverse low-income job seekers, adapting framing by community. Build sustained relationships with board members and system partners over time, recognizing that trust- and funding-influence take months or years to develop. Work to influence board funding priorities, positioning IRC Montana to draw down multi-year, public-sector workforce funding as a stable complement to grant-based revenue. Community & Employer Relationship Building Identify, cultivate, and maintain relationships with employers, donors, career service providers, registered apprenticeship providers, small business and corporate entities, educational institutions, and financial experts and mentors to expand client opportunities. Build relationships with the Montana Department of Labor & Industry, community colleges, and vocational training providers. Represent IRC Montana at community events and coalitions; maintain an up-to-date partner map and relationship status across the state, in coordination with office leadership. Geographic Expansion Develop a strategy for identifying and prioritizing new geographic areas for program expansion, informed by population needs, labor market data, and funder priorities. Travel regularly to new and existing communities to conduct outreach, needs assessments, and relationship-building ahead of program launch. Adapt program design to local conditions and build local partnerships before or alongside rollout in each new area. Client Services & Outcomes Oversee delivery of job readiness training, placement support, and retention services, ensuring they are culturally responsive and accessible (addressing language, transportation, and documentation-related barriers) Track individual client outcomes and aggregate program data for funder and organizational reporting. Team & Operational Leadership Hire, train, and manage staff supporting the program as it grows; collaborate as an active member of the office leadership team. Represent IRC Montana in public, professional, and governmental forums; lead planning of special events such as partner engagement events and client workshops. In coordination with office leadership, develop and monitor department, program, and grant budgets, and implement process improvements as the program grows. Ensure compliance with funder requirements across federal, state, and foundation-funded grants. Leadership, Coordination & Role Clarity Serve as the Executive Director's point person for workforce development programming and priorities. Implement decisions and priorities set by the Executive Director and technical team input as they relate to workforce development. Ensure clear role boundaries, shared planning, and consistent communication with site leadership and other program staff to avoid duplication of effort. Participate in regional leadership meetings and organizational forums as requested. Comply with all IRC policies, procedures, and protocols. Perform other duties as assigned by the Executive Director. Data, Reporting & Continuous Improvement Establish data collection systems suited to a new program, and regularly report performance to leadership and funders. Document lessons learned as the program expands, to make replication in new geographic areas progressively easier. Key Working Relationships Position Reports to: Executive Director, IRC Montana Manages: Program staff, interns, and volunteers supporting workforce development services, as the program grows. Internal: IRC Montana program staff and leadership, Operations, Finance, HR, Mountain West regional leadership, and relevant HQ teams. External: Workforce development boards, employers, community colleges, apprenticeship providers and training providers, community partners, and local stakeholders. Job Requirements University degree (four-year, B.A.) required; advanced degree in a related field preferred. Minimum 3-5 years of related program experience, including program development, monitoring, and evaluation. Experience designing or launching workforce development, employment, or job readiness programs, ideally within a nonprofit or public-sector context. Experience engaging with public workforce systems (e.g., workforce development boards, WIOA-funded programs) strongly preferred. Previous fundraising and grant writing experience. Demonstrated success building and sustaining relationships with employers, government agencies, or community institutions, with comfort in relationship-building processes that unfold over months or years. Highly organized self-starter able to manage multiple priorities and deliver results independently in a fast-paced environment — particularly suited to building a new program from scratch. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including comfort representing the organization publicly; fluent in English, with a second language desirable. At locations in Berlin-Buch, Berlin-Mitte, Heidelberg and Mannheim, our researchers harness interdisciplinary collaboration to decipher the complexities of disease at the systems level – from molecules and cells to organs and the entire organism. Through academic, clinical, and industry partnerships, as well as global networks, we strive to translate biological discoveries into applications that enable the early detection of deviations from health, personalize treatment, and ultimately prevent disease. First founded in 1992, the Max Delbrück Center today inspires and nurtures a diverse talent pool of 1,800 people from over 70 countries. We are 90 percent funded by the German federal government and 10 percent by the state of Berlin. The research group of Prof. Karina Yaniv at the Helmholtz Institute for Translational AngioCardioScience (HI-TAC) is looking for a motivated and team-oriented Bioinformatician (f/m/d) to join its growing interdisciplinary research team. As a newly established laboratory, we offer a unique opportunity to actively contribute to shaping an ambitious research program from the outset. In a dynamic and international environment, bioinformaticians and experimental researchers work closely together to address key questions in vascular biology and develop novel therapeutic approaches. Our research focuses on the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying blood and lymphatic vessel development, tissue regeneration, and vascular diseases. To address these questions, we combine state-of-the-art approaches, including single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, epigenomics, imaging, functional genetics, and computational biology. As a Bioinformatician (f/m/d), you will work closely with experimental researchers and contribute to projects throughout the entire research process—from study design and data processing to statistical analysis and biological interpretation. review_candidates.description: With over 58 stores and the largest avocational cooking program in the US, Sur La Table offers an unsurpassed selection of exclusive and premium-quality goods for the kitchen and table – and the culinary expertise and inspiration to go along with it. This position combines strategic business acumen with strong operational expertise to drive both culinary and retail business performance while delivering #bestincenter service, a company-wide standard for excellence in service. Key Responsibilities Leadership & Team Development Recruit, develop and retain a high-performing team to meet the business needs of both culinary and retail. Lead, coach, and inspire associates to exceed performance expectations and uphold a positive team culture. Customer Experience & Brand Representation Represent Sur La Table’s brand and culture by creating memorable, educational experiences that inspire repeat visits and customer loyalty. Maintains expertise by staying current on products, actively engaging in available training, and independently seeking out additional resources. Ensure exceptional customer experience by leading a customer-focused, Guest Obsessed culture. Address customer concerns and resolve issues in a timely manner to maintain satisfaction and loyalty. Sales & Business Performance Develop and implement strategies, including effective merchandising, marketing, and customer engagement, to exceed sales and financial goals across culinary and retail operations. Monitor and analyze key performance metrics daily to identify opportunities and optimize store performance. Consistently meet or exceed culinary and retail goals by delivering exceptional classes and customer experiences that drive engagement and sales. Performance is measured by key KPIs such as second-class sign-ups, retail product sales, individual sales volume, average transaction value, customer conversion rates, and guest feedback through Google reviews. Operations & Compliance Oversee daily store operations, ensuring compliance with company policies and procedures. Maintain accurate inventory levels, minimize shrink, and ensure proper product merchandising. Ensure store safety and cleanliness, addressing any maintenance needs promptly. Maintains the accuracy and integrity of associates’ records, including but not limited to time and attendance data, food safety certifications, and personal information. Adhere to applicable wage and hour laws. Accurately records time worked according to SLT Policy. Models and ensures all Sur La Table policies and standard operating procedures (SOPs) are communicated effectively to associates, maintained and consistently followed. Physical Requirements Ability to communicate verbally and work cooperatively with associates and customers. Ability to remain standing for up to 5 hours at a time. Ability to move about the store coaching and directing associates; selling to customers and retrieving merchandise from stockroom or sales floor. Ability to grab, reach, push, pull, bend, stoop, kneel, and crouch to retrieve and replenish merchandise from stockroom or sales floor. Ability to lift and/or move merchandise weighing up to 50 lbs. Ability to ascend/descend ladders to retrieve and/or move merchandise. Ability to operate a computer, POS system, keyboards, merchandise scanners and mouse to accomplish work. Workweeks are expected to be between 46 and 48 hours with the ability to have a flexible schedule, including nights, weekends, and holidays. Regular and predictable attendance. Qualifications & Experience Must be 21 years of age or older at the time of employment. 3+ years of retail management experience, preferably in a specialty or culinary retail environment. Current Food Manager Certification, or ability to acquire certification as needed Proven track record of achieving sales and motivating high performing sales teams while meeting operational goals. Strong leadership skills with the ability to inspire, develop, and retain a high performing team. Excellent communication, problem-solving, and decision-making abilities. new_matches.title: Sr Infrastructure Engineer
new_matches.description: The Senior Infrastructure Engineer serves as the designated backup and knowledge-continuity resource for Baylor Genetics’ on-premises data center and network environment. This role exists to ensure uninterrupted operation of the critical infrastructure supporting our genomics pipeline and clinical laboratory systems, and to eliminate single points of failure in IT operations. This role may evolve as organizational needs change. Exists to sustain, document, and be fully capable of independently operating all core on-premises infrastructure — servers, storage, networking, and security systems — in any operational scenario, including emergency coverage of the primary infrastructure lead. Impacts clinical laboratory operations, genomics pipeline throughput, and the reliability of all on-premises and hybrid-connected systems used across the organization. Success looks like: zero unplanned outages attributable to single-person dependency, a fully documented environment with up-to-date runbooks, and the demonstrated ability to assume full infrastructure ownership without disruption. Key Responsibilities Serve as the designated backup for the primary infrastructure lead — assume full operational control of data center, network, and server environments during absences, emergencies, or transitions to ensure zero service interruption. Administer and maintain physical and virtual server infrastructure (Windows Server, Linux, VMware/Hyper-V), including provisioning, patching, performance monitoring, and capacity planning to sustain 99.9%+ uptime. Manage LAN/WAN networking operations including switches, routers, firewalls, and VLANs to maintain high availability and security across all on-premises systems. Build, maintain, and continuously improve runbooks, network diagrams, and disaster recovery documentation to eliminate single points of failure and reduce mean time to recovery. Support and sustain the on-premises genomics pipeline infrastructure, ensuring compute and storage resources meet demanding throughput and availability requirements for clinical laboratory operations. Collaborate cross-functionally with bioinformatics, clinical lab, and IT teams to align infrastructure reliability with patient-impacting laboratory workflows. Proactively identify and remediate risks including aging hardware, technical debt, and configuration vulnerabilities — presenting actionable proposals to leadership. Respond to infrastructure incidents and outages with urgency, including after-hours escalations, to minimize downtime impact on laboratory and clinical operations. Perform other duties as assigned to support team and organizational objectives. Comply with all company policies, procedures, and applicable regulatory requirements. Qualifications Required Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field; or equivalent technical training and experience. 7+ years of hands-on enterprise IT infrastructure engineering experience in a complex, predominantly on-premises environment. Deep expertise in physical and virtual server administration (Windows Server 2016/2019/2022, Linux) including VMware vSphere or Microsoft Hyper-V. Strong networking fundamentals: routing, switching, VLANs, firewall policy management, and systematic network troubleshooting (Cisco, Palo Alto, Fortinet, or equivalent). Experience managing physical data center environments — rack/stack, structured cabling, power, and cooling awareness. Proficiency with SAN/NAS storage platforms and enterprise backup/recovery systems (Veeam, Commvault, or equivalent). Working knowledge of Microsoft 365 and Azure Active Directory in a hybrid on-premises/cloud context. Strong documentation discipline: ability to produce clear runbooks, network diagrams, and standard operating procedures independently. Proven ability to rapidly learn complex, undocumented environments and operate independently under high-pressure conditions. Equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered. Preferred Experience in a healthcare, clinical laboratory, genomics, or other regulated life sciences environment. 7+ years of progressive experience in enterprise infrastructure roles with demonstrated ownership of critical systems. Relevant certifications: CCNA/CCNP, VCP-DCV, MCSE, CompTIA Network+/Security+, or equivalent. Familiarity with HPC or high-throughput bioinformatics pipeline infrastructure. Exposure to HIPAA compliance requirements, NIST frameworks, or SOC 2 audit environments. Scripting proficiency (PowerShell, Bash, or Python) for infrastructure automation and administrative efficiency. Experience with monitoring platforms such as PRTG, SolarWinds, Zabbix, or similar tools. COMPETENCIES Advanced systems and network troubleshooting — able to diagnose and resolve complex infrastructure issues across server, storage, and network layers independently. Infrastructure documentation and knowledge transfer — consistently produces clear, actionable runbooks and SOPs that allow others to execute without prior context. Operational resilience under pressure — calm, methodical decision-making during incidents and outages in environments where downtime directly impacts patient care. Cross-functional collaboration — effectively partners with bioinformatics, clinical lab, and IT teams to align infrastructure performance with organizational mission. Proactive risk identification — anticipates infrastructure vulnerabilities and aging hardware risks, and drives remediation before failures occur. PHYSICAL DEMANDS AND WORK ENVIRONMENT Location: Houston, TX. This position is a hybrid work environment. Most work can be done remotely but must have the ability to arrive on-site at our Houston Location in a reasonable amount of time if necessary. Must be able to lift and move equipment up to 50 lbs; perform physical tasks in a data center environment including rack/stack of servers and network hardware. Ability to work in environments with variable temperatures (data center cooling), moderate noise levels, and continuous standing or walking during data center operations. Occasional after-hours availability required for scheduled maintenance windows, incident response, and emergency infrastructure coverage. Must be authorized to work in the United States; visa sponsorship is not available for this position. No regular travel required; occasional travel to offsite data center or disaster recovery locations may arise. Main Accountabilities But Not Limited To The Following Leadership and Management Plans and prioritises own activities, which span across a range of different work streams or internal client relationships. Responds to changing and at times competing requirements to ensure effective delivery of responsibilities over set reporting timescales. Provide a good standard of financial business partnering, financial insight and financial discipline. Provide line management and task coordination to the Accountant based in Ethiopia, ensuring consistent standards of delivery and compliance. Financial Management Work closely with the MSP to deliver retained P2P, O2C, R2R and CLM financial processes in Ethiopia and other countries in cluster 2, ensuring consistent, accurate and robust financial accounting in line with accounting practices and corporate policies. Support month-end and year-end close processes, balance-sheet reconciliations and maintenance of the general ledger. Lead country-level tax reporting and compliance activities in Ethiopia, working alongside the Tax & Statutory CoE team and under direction of the FC – SSA Cluster 2 . Prepare local tax submissions and statutory filings, ensure timely compliance with Ethiopian tax authorities, timely application for VAT refunds and provide tax insights to senior colleagues. Identify and escalate material tax risks or regulatory changes as they arise. Contribute to statutory reporting working closely with the CoE – Statutory & Tax team and the Financial Controller – Cluster 2 to ensure accurate and compliant reporting Relationship and Stakeholder Management Develop good working relationships with key internal customers, colleagues and the MSP to ensure that activities comply with professional accounting standards, technical accounting guidance and other external reporting requirements in British Council. As required, represent the British Council in discussions and dealings with external suppliers/providers and local authorities in Ethiopia & Cluster 2. Support business unit leads and operations teams in Ethiopia & Cluster 2 to embed new finance ways of working post-transformation. Provide practical guidance on MSP-supported P2P, CLM, O2C and R2R processes, and respond to finance queries from operational colleagues, escalating to the FC – SSA Cluster 2 as appropriate. Sector/Subject Expertise Proactively maintains a sound working knowledge of developments in external policy, practice and regulation within financial accounting, including statutory, banking, and tax requirements, to build credibility, confidence and business insight Ethiopia & Cluster 2. Provide first-line advice and guidance on financial accounting and tax issues; liaise with senior colleagues and specialist finance functions including Tax, Treasury, Finance Policy and Global Process Owners as needed. Pro-actively identify unusual or complex transactions, discuss with senior colleagues and support action to resolve issues. Service Improvement Support the implementation of new or updated accounting and reporting requirements in line with IFRS and professional accounting standards in Ethiopia. Support work to centralise and move activity to an MSP environment and embed the Phase 2 controllership model in-country. Requirements Of The Role Minimum 2 years of experience in operational financial management and/or management accounting. Degree level education. Part qualified with a recognised accounting body. Written and verbal proficiency in English is required. Written and verbal proficiency in Amharic is also required for this role based in Ethiopia. Financial reporting and tax compliance experience. Advanced experience of Excel. ERP systems experience (transaction level and reporting). Desirable Minimum 2 years of experience in operational financial management and/or management accounting. Experience working with SAP. Experience of working in an international organisation. A connected and trusted UK in a more connected and trusted world. Equality, Diversity and Inclusion Statement We are committed to equality, diversity and inclusion and welcome applications from all sections of the community as we believe that a diverse workforce gives added depth to our work. The British Council is a Disability Confident Employer. The Disability Confident scheme helps challenge attitudes, increase understanding of disability and ensure staff are drawn from the widest possible pool of talent. We guarantee an interview for disabled applicants who meet the minimum role requirements. We welcome discussions about specific requirements or adjustments to enable participation and engagement in our work and activities. Safeguarding Statement The British Council is committed to safeguarding children, young people and adults who we work with. We believe that all children and adults everywhere in the world deserve to live in safe environments and have the right to be protected from all forms of abuse, maltreatment and exploitation as set out in article 19, UNCRC (United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child) 1989. Appointment to positions where there is direct involvement with vulnerable groups will be dependent on thorough checks being completed in line with legal requirements and with the British Council’s Safeguarding policies for Adults and Children. new_matches.title: Program Officer (Eye Health Project Coordinator)
new_matches.description: Job D About The Job Program Officer – Eye Health Project Coordinator Project Title Seeing the Future: Strengthening Ophthalmic Services in Oromia, Sidama, Central Ethiopia, South Ethiopia and Amhara Regional States Job Title Program Officer (Eye Health Project Coordinator) Project Number P10625 Contract Duration One (1) year, renewable subject to performance and availability of funds Number of Positions One (1) Location Addis Ababa (with frequent travel to Oromia, Sidama, Central Ethiopia, South Ethiopia, and Amhara regions) Reports To Program Director Application Deadline 10 working days from the date of this announcement Organizational Background Cheshire Ethiopia (Registration No. 0505) is a leading national non-governmental organization committed to disability rehabilitation and inclusive health services since 1962. Its mission is to empower persons with disabilities to participate fully in society through comprehensive and coordinated rehabilitation and health services. With a decentralized structure spanning five strategic locations across the country, Cheshire Ethiopia operates with a team of 210 professionals and non-professional staff, maintaining robust governance, administrative, financial, and procurement processes that meet national and donor requirements. Cheshire Ethiopia, in collaboration with CBM International, is implementing the “Seeing the Future” project a three-year initiative (April 2025 to March 2028) aimed at strengthening inclusive ophthalmic services in underserved regions of Ethiopia. The project targets the reduction of preventable blindness and visual impairment through infrastructure development, community outreach, health worker training, and public awareness campaigns. Position Purpose The Program Officer – Eye Health Project Coordinator will serve as the primary operational focal person for the “Seeing the Future” project. While holding the organizational title of Program Officer in line with Cheshire Ethiopia’s job grading structure, the incumbent will function in the overall capacity of a Project Coordinator, responsible for the day-to-day planning, coordination, implementation, monitoring, and reporting of all project activities across the target regions. The position requires a dynamic professional with strong project management competencies, sound understanding of health program implementation, and a genuine commitment to disability-inclusive development. The Program Officer will work closely with regional eye health teams, partner hospitals, government health offices, and CBM Ethiopia to ensure timely, quality, and inclusive delivery of project results. Key Responsibilities and Duties Project Planning and Implementation Leads the development and regular updating of detailed annual work plans, activity schedules, and procurement plans in alignment with the project document (PPA) and donor requirements. Coordinates and oversees field-level implementation of all project activities across Oromia, Sidama, Central Ethiopia, South Ethiopia, and Amhara regional states. Facilitates the setup, renovation, and operationalization of eye care facilities at Menagesha Secondary Eye Unit and Hawassa Primary Eye Care Center. Oversees the establishment and functioning of the optical manufacturing workshop and dispensary at Hawassa, including procurement of raw materials such as lenses and frames. Coordinates mobile outreach visits to remote and underserved villages in collaboration with government health facilities and satellite units. Ensures the project adopts a disability-inclusive, gender-sensitive, and rights-based approach in all activities. Performa other similar duties as assigned by the program Director Stakeholder Coordination and Liaison Serves as the principal point of contact for project stakeholders, including CBM Ethiopia Country Office, regional health bureaus, woreda health offices, partner hospitals (e.g., ALERT), and community leaders. Facilitates regular coordination meetings, joint planning sessions, and review forums with governmental and non-governmental partners. Represents Cheshire Ethiopia in relevant technical working groups, health cluster meetings, and eye health coordination platforms per the directive of the program Director Maintains strong working relationships with satellite primary health care facilities (21 facilities targeted) to strengthen screening, referral, and primary-level eye care capacities. Capacity Building and Training Coordination Organizes and coordinates training workshops for health extension workers, optometrists, ophthalmic nurses, and clinical nurses on basic and inclusive eye care based on WHO guidelines. Facilitates training for community rehabilitation workers and school teachers on identification of eye conditions and referral pathways. Supports the development of training materials, guidelines, and eye care capacity-building packages in collaboration with partner hospitals. Coordinates World Sight Day events, community-based awareness campaigns, and school-based eye health screening activities. Community Engagement and Awareness Designs and implements community-based awareness programs using local media, schools, community centers, and faith-based organizations. Ensures the distribution of educational materials on eye health, common eye diseases, and preventive measures across target communities. Establishes and maintains community feedback mechanisms and ensure that the voices of persons with disabilities, women, and marginalized groups are incorporated into program delivery. Conducts rapid assessments and community mapping to identify high-need areas, target groups, and referral linkages. Monitoring, Evaluation, and Reporting Implements project monitoring systems and ensure regular tracking of performance indicators including consultation targets (52,500), cataract surgeries (5,000), eyeglasses distribution (13,500), and outreach visits (10). Collects, verifies, and analyzes project data to assess progress against targets and outcomes; prepare data-driven reports and case studies. Conducts and supports regular field monitoring visits (minimum 9 over project duration) and document findings with corrective action plans. Coordinates the project kickoff workshop, annual stakeholders’ review and learning forums, and final evaluation. Prepares high-quality monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, and annual project progress reports for internal and donor use in compliance with CBM reporting standards. Financial and Resource Management Supports preparation of annual budgets and participate in budget revision processes in coordination with the Finance team. Monitors project expenditure against approved budgets and flag variances promptly to the Program Manager and Finance unit. Oversees efficient management and utilization of project resources including vehicles, medical equipment, optical supplies, and office materials. Ensures compliance with Cheshire Ethiopia’s financial policies, procurement procedures, and CBM financial management guidelines. Compliance, Risk, and Safeguarding Ensures full compliance with legal, regulatory, organizational, and donor requirements throughout project implementation. Identifies, documents, and escalates project risks; develops and monitors implementation of risk mitigation plans. Upholds and promotes Cheshire Ethiopia’s safeguarding, child protection, and do-no-harm policies in all activities. Ensuree health and safety protocols are followed during clinical and outreach activities. Documentation and Knowledge Management Maintains systematic and accurate records of project activities, beneficiary data, financial transactions, and correspondence. Documents lessons learned, best practices, and success stories for organizational learning and external communication. Contributes to knowledge-sharing platforms and support the development of project briefs, case studies, and donor communication materials. Working Conditions The position is based at Cheshire Ethiopia’s head office in Addis Ababa, with frequent field travel required across project operational areas in Oromia, Sidama and South Ethiopia, Central Ethiopia, and Amhara regional states. The post holder must be prepared for travel to remote and rural areas under varying field conditions. Salary and benefits are set according to Cheshire Ethiopia’s organizational salary scale for the Program Officer grade. The initial contract duration is one (1) year, renewable subject to satisfactory performance, project needs, and availability of funds as outlined in the project budget. Equal Opportunity Statement Cheshire Ethiopia is an equal opportunity employer. We warmly welcome applications from all qualified individuals regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, religion, or disability status. Women and persons with disabilities are strongly encouraged to apply. Cheshire Ethiopia is committed to a workplace free from discrimination and dedicated to the principles of inclusion and diversity. About You Education Master of Public Health (MPH), Master of Science in Health Sciences, Master in Project Management, or a related field — Minimum 5 years of relevant experience. OR Bachelor’s Degree in Public Health, Optometry, Health Officer, or related health/development discipline — Minimum 7 years of relevant experience. Professional Experience Proven experience in coordinating or managing health or development projects at program officer, project coordinator, or equivalent level in an NGO setting. Experience in multi-regional project implementation and working with government health structures (regional health bureaus, woredas, health facilities). Solid financial literacy and ability to manage budgets, review expenditure reports, and ensure financial accountability. Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English; proficiency in Amharic is required; knowledge of additional regional languages is an advantage. Proficiency in MS Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint); experience with project management tools is a plus. Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making abilities. Ability to work collaboratively in a multidisciplinary team and manage relationships with diverse stakeholders. High level of initiative, accountability, and ability to work under pressure while meeting deadlines. Willingness and ability to undertake frequent travel to remote and underserved areas across multiple regional states. new_matches.title: General Manager (Sur La Table)
new_matches.description: With over 58 stores and the largest avocational cooking program in the US, Sur La Table offers an unsurpassed selection of exclusive and premium-quality goods for the kitchen and table – and the culinary expertise and inspiration to go along with it. Whether the job entails interacting with our customers, driving digital growth, or providing vital behind-the-scenes support, we’re all here for the same reason – to roll up our sleeves and create happiness through cooking and sharing good food. Position Overview As a General Manager at Sur La Table, you play a key role in the success of the store by leading high-performing retail and culinary teams that inspires customers throughout every stage of their culinary experience. This position combines strategic business acumen with strong operational expertise to drive both culinary and retail business performance while delivering #bestincenter service, a company-wide standard for excellence in service. Key Responsibilities Leadership & Team Development Recruit, develop and retain a high-performing team to meet the business needs of both culinary and retail. Lead, coach, and inspire associates to exceed performance expectations and uphold a positive team culture. Conduct regular performance evaluations, provide feedback, and create development plans to support individual and team growth. Customer Experience & Brand Representation Represent Sur La Table’s brand and culture by creating memorable, educational experiences that inspire repeat visits and customer loyalty. Maintains expertise by staying current on products, actively engaging in available training, and independently seeking out additional resources. Ensure exceptional customer experience by leading a customer-focused, Guest Obsessed culture. Address customer concerns and resolve issues in a timely manner to maintain satisfaction and loyalty. Sales & Business Performance Develop and implement strategies, including effective merchandising, marketing, and customer engagement, to exceed sales and financial goals across culinary and retail operations. Monitor and analyze key performance metrics daily to identify opportunities and optimize store performance. Consistently meet or exceed culinary and retail goals by delivering exceptional classes and customer experiences that drive engagement and sales. Performance is measured by key KPIs such as second-class sign-ups, retail product sales, individual sales volume, average transaction value, customer conversion rates, and guest feedback through Google reviews. Operations & Compliance Oversee daily store operations, ensuring compliance with company policies and procedures. Maintain accurate inventory levels, minimize shrink, and ensure proper product merchandising. Ensure store safety and cleanliness, addressing any maintenance needs promptly. Maintains the accuracy and integrity of associates’ records, including but not limited to time and attendance data, food safety certifications, and personal information. Adhere to applicable wage and hour laws. Accurately records time worked according to SLT Policy. Models and ensures all Sur La Table policies and standard operating procedures (SOPs) are communicated effectively to associates, maintained and consistently followed. Physical Requirements Ability to communicate verbally and work cooperatively with associates and customers. Ability to remain standing for up to 5 hours at a time. Ability to move about the store coaching and directing associates; selling to customers and retrieving merchandise from stockroom or sales floor. Ability to grab, reach, push, pull, bend, stoop, kneel, and crouch to retrieve and replenish merchandise from stockroom or sales floor. Ability to lift and/or move merchandise weighing up to 50 lbs. Ability to ascend/descend ladders to retrieve and/or move merchandise. Ability to operate a computer, POS system, keyboards, merchandise scanners and mouse to accomplish work. Workweeks are expected to be between 46 and 48 hours with the ability to have a flexible schedule, including nights, weekends, and holidays. Regular and predictable attendance. Qualifications & Experience Must be 21 years of age or older at the time of employment. 3+ years of retail management experience, preferably in a specialty or culinary retail environment. Current Food Manager Certification, or ability to acquire certification as needed Proven track record of achieving sales and motivating high performing sales teams while meeting operational goals. Strong leadership skills with the ability to inspire, develop, and retain a high performing team. Excellent communication, problem-solving, and decision-making abilities. Passion for community engagement and providing exceptional customer experiences. Key ResponsibilitiesBusiness Development Develop and execute UK-GCC Private Capital's business development strategy across the United Kingdom. Build and manage a high-value pipeline of prospective clients, members, sponsors, exhibitors, investors and strategic partners. Originate new revenue opportunities across private capital, real estate, financial services, wealth management, technology, infrastructure, energy transition and other investment sectors. Lead senior-level meetings, presentations, proposals and commercial negotiations. Develop relationships with major UK corporates, investment firms, financial institutions and professional services organisations. Identify opportunities to expand existing commercial relationships. Develop measurable revenue targets and maintain a disciplined commercial pipeline. Provide regular reporting on opportunities, conversions, revenues and market intelligence. Capital Formation A core part of the mandate will be identifying businesses, investment managers, funds and real estate opportunities seeking institutional and private capital. Develop relationships with private equity, private credit, venture capital, infrastructure and real estate investment managers. Recruit real estate developers, investment managers and project owners to participate in the Real Estate Exhibition. Develop relationships with organisations seeking direct access to private capital and institutional investors. Secure commercial participation through sponsorships, exhibition packages, memberships and strategic partnerships. Identify appropriate senior executives for speaking and thought-leadership opportunities. Develop long-term commercial relationships with participating organisations beyond individual summits. UK-GCC Cross-Border Opportunities Originate investment and commercial opportunities connecting UK businesses and investment managers with GCC capital. Build relationships with UK organisations seeking expansion into Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain and Oman. Identify opportunities involving capital raising, investment, joint ventures, strategic partnerships and market entry. Connect appropriate UK opportunities with UK-GCC Private Capital's international investor network. Develop strategic relationships with organisations supporting UK-GCC trade, investment and capital flows. Represent UK-GCC Private Capital at relevant conferences, investment meetings and industry events. Strategic Relationship & Account Management Build trusted, long-term relationships with members, sponsors, investors, developers and institutional partners. Maintain senior-level engagement with key accounts. Identify opportunities to increase revenue and deepen relationships across the platform. Ensure strategic partners and members receive ongoing commercial value. Maintain accurate CRM records, prospect information and revenue pipelines. new_matches.title: Director Business Development France
new_matches.description: Director of Business Development France Paris France | UK-GCC Private Capital About UK-GCC Private Capital UK-GCC Private Capital is an international strategic platform for LPs and GPs, private equity firms, sovereign wealth funds, venture capital firms, family offices, institutional investors, investment funds, real estate investors and growth-driven businesses across France, the UK, GCC and international markets. Through our investment summits, membership platform, investor network and strategic relationships, we create opportunities for capital formation, investment, partnerships and cross-border business. The Role UK-GCC Private Capital is seeking an exceptional Director of France Business Development to lead commercial growth, capital formation and strategic relationship development across France. This is a senior, revenue-focused role for a highly connected and entrepreneurial business development professional with strong relationships across France's private capital, investment, real estate, wealth management and financial services ecosystem. The Director will be responsible for originating and converting high-value opportunities across: Capital formation and fundraising mandates Annual corporate and institutional memberships Investment Summit sponsorships Real Estate Exhibition participation Strategic and commercial partnerships Investor and institutional relationships Cross-border France–UK–GCC investment opportunities Real estate project and investment opportunities The successful candidate must be capable of engaging directly with CEOs, founders, CIOs, managing partners, investment directors, heads of capital formation, investor relations professionals and other senior decision-makers. This is not a traditional sales role . We are looking for an individual who can open doors, build trusted C-suite relationships, originate opportunities, negotiate commercial agreements and convert relationships into measurable revenue. Key ResponsibilitiesBusiness Development & Revenue Generation Develop and execute UK-GCC Private Capital's business development strategy across France. Build and manage a high-value pipeline of prospective clients, members, sponsors, exhibitors, investors and strategic partners. Originate new revenue opportunities across private capital, real estate, financial services, wealth management, technology, infrastructure, energy transition and other investment sectors. Lead senior-level meetings, presentations, proposals and commercial negotiations. Develop relationships with major French corporates, investment firms, financial institutions and professional services organisations. Identify opportunities to expand existing commercial relationships. Develop measurable revenue targets and maintain a disciplined commercial pipeline. Provide regular reporting on opportunities, conversions, revenues and market intelligence. Build relationships across Paris, Lyon and other major French business and investment centres. Capital Formation A core part of the mandate will be identifying French businesses, investment managers, funds and real estate opportunities seeking institutional and private capital. The Director will: Originate capital-raising and capital formation mandates. Develop relationships with private equity, private credit, venture capital, infrastructure and real estate investment managers in France. Identify French businesses and investment opportunities seeking access to UK, GCC and international capital. Facilitate introductions to relevant family offices, sovereign investors, investment funds and institutional capital. Support fundraising discussions, investor engagement and strategic introductions. Identify opportunities for equity, private credit, co-investment, joint ventures and other investment structures. Build long-term relationships with clients beyond individual transactions. Identify French companies seeking international expansion, strategic investment or access to GCC markets. Membership Development The Director will lead the growth of UK-GCC Private Capital's annual membership base within France. Target organisations will include: Private equity and private credit firms Venture capital firms Asset and investment managers Family offices Wealth management businesses Banks and financial institutions Real estate developers and investment companies Infrastructure and energy businesses Technology and growth companies Professional and advisory firms French corporates seeking international investment and market access Other organisations seeking access to France–UK–GCC private capital relationships The Director will identify suitable organisations, engage senior decision-makers, present the membership proposition and convert qualified prospects into long-term members. Investment Summits & Real Estate Exhibition The Director will play a major commercial role in the growth of the UK-GCC Private Capital Investment Summits and Real Estate Exhibition . Responsibilities include: Secure leading French and international organisations as sponsors, exhibitors, delegates and strategic partners. Recruit French real estate developers, investment managers and project owners to participate in the Real Estate Exhibition. Develop relationships with organisations seeking direct access to private capital and institutional investors. Secure commercial participation through sponsorships, exhibition packages, memberships and strategic partnerships. Identify appropriate senior executives for speaking and thought-leadership opportunities. Develop long-term commercial relationships with participating organisations beyond individual summits. Promote participation from French investors, developers, funds, corporates and professional services firms. France–UK–GCC Cross-Border Opportunities Originate investment and commercial opportunities connecting French businesses and investment managers with UK, GCC and international capital. Build relationships with French organisations seeking expansion into Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain and Oman. Identify opportunities involving capital raising, investment, joint ventures, strategic partnerships and market entry. Connect appropriate French opportunities with UK-GCC Private Capital's international investor network. Identify GCC investment opportunities for French companies, funds, developers and strategic investors. Develop strategic relationships with organisations supporting France–UK–GCC trade, investment and capital flows. Represent UK-GCC Private Capital at relevant French and international conferences, investment meetings and industry events. Strategic Relationship & Account Management Build trusted, long-term relationships with members, sponsors, investors, developers and institutional partners. Maintain senior-level engagement with key accounts across France. Identify opportunities to increase revenue and deepen relationships across the platform. Ensure strategic partners and members receive ongoing commercial value. Maintain accurate CRM records, prospect information and revenue pipelines. Act as a senior ambassador for UK-GCC Private Capital in the French market. Develop relationships with relevant French business associations, investment networks, chambers of commerce and institutional organisations. What We Are Looking For We are looking for a commercially driven and highly credible French business development professional who already possesses a strong network within France's investment and business community. Essential Experience Strong track record in business development, capital formation, investment, real estate, financial services, wealth management, asset management, private markets or a closely related sector. Established network of senior decision-makers across France. Demonstrated ability to originate and close high-value commercial opportunities. Experience engaging with private equity firms, investment funds, family offices, institutional investors, real estate businesses, banks, wealth managers and/or major corporates. Ability to engage confidently with CEOs, founders, CIOs, managing partners and other senior executives. Experience developing new markets, client relationships and revenue pipelines. Strong commercial negotiation and relationship-management capabilities. Understanding of private capital, investment and cross-border business. Excellent communication, presentation and stakeholder-management skills. Fluency in French and strong professional English. Knowledge of GCC markets, investors and business culture would be highly advantageous. Entrepreneurial approach and ability to operate independently. Strong commercial judgement with a demonstrable record of generating measurable revenue. What Success Looks Like Within the first 12–24 months, the Director will be expected to: Build a substantial French commercial and capital formation pipeline. Generate significant new revenue for UK-GCC Private Capital. Secure new annual corporate and institutional members in France. Originate capital-raising and investment mandates involving French businesses and investment managers. Secure French sponsors and exhibitors for UK-GCC Private Capital Investment Summits. Bring leading French real estate developers and investment businesses into the Real Estate Exhibition. Establish relationships with major French investment funds, family offices, private equity firms, wealth managers and institutional investors. Generate new France–UK–GCC cross-border investment and commercial opportunities. Develop long-term strategic partnerships with French organisations and institutions. Increase UK-GCC Private Capital's profile and market presence across France. Build a strong network across Paris, Lyon and other relevant French investment and business centres. Apply If you are a high-performing French business development professional with an established network across private capital, investment, real estate, wealth management or financial services , we would like to hear from you. new_matches.title: Assistant Store Manager (Sur La Table)
new_matches.description: With over 58 stores and the largest avocational cooking program in the US, Sur La Table offers an unsurpassed selection of exclusive and premium-quality goods for the kitchen and table – and the culinary expertise and inspiration to go along with it. Whether the job entails interacting with our customers, driving digital growth, or providing vital behind-the-scenes support, we’re all here for the same reason – to roll up our sleeves and create happiness through cooking and sharing good food. Position Overview As an Assistant Store Manager at Sur La Table, you play a key role in the success of the store by assisting a high-performing retail team that inspires customers throughout every stage of their culinary experience. The Assistant Store Manager helps cultivate a positive store culture focused on #bestincenter service, a company-wide standard for excellence in service. Key Responsibilities Leadership & Team Development Supports the recruitment, training, and ongoing development of a high-performing team to meet the business needs of both culinary and retail. Provide coaching and feedback to ensure team members deliver outstanding customer experience. Assist in development plans to support individual and team growth. Customer Experience & Brand Representation Represent Sur La Table’s brand and culture by creating memorable, educational experiences that inspire repeat visits and customer loyalty. Maintains expertise by staying current on products, actively engaging in available training, and independently seeking out additional resources. Ensure exceptional customer experience by leading a customer-focused, Guest Obsessed culture. Address customer concerns and resolve issues in a timely manner to maintain satisfaction and loyalty. Sales & Business Performance Partners with the General/Store Manager in developing and implementing strategies, including effective merchandising, marketing, and customer engagement, to exceed sales and financial goals across culinary and retail operations. Analyze daily performance metrics, apply insights to drive results, and lead follow-ups with the team to ensure execution. Consistently meet or exceed monthly sales goals, contributing to overall store revenue. Performance is measured by key KPIs such as individual sales volume, average transaction value, and customer conversion rates. Operations & Compliance Assist with daily store operations, ensuring compliance with company policies and procedures. Maintain accurate inventory levels, minimize shrink, and ensure proper product merchandising. Ensure store safety and cleanliness, addressing any maintenance needs promptly. Assist with maintaining the accuracy and integrity of associate records, including but not limited to time and attendance data, food safety certifications, and personal information. Adhere to applicable wage and hour laws. Accurately records time worked according to SLT Policy. Models and ensures all Sur La Table policies and standard operating procedures (SOPs) are communicated effectively to associates, maintained and consistently followed. Physical Requirements Ability to communicate verbally and work cooperatively with associates and customers. Ability to remain standing for up to 5 hours at a time. Ability to move about the store coaching and directing associates; selling to customers and retrieving merchandise from stockroom or sales floor. Ability to grab, reach, push, pull, bend, stoop, kneel, and crouch to retrieve and replenish merchandise from stockroom or sales floor. Ability to lift and/or move merchandise weighing up to 50 lbs. Ability to ascend/descend ladders to retrieve and/or move merchandise. Ability to operate a computer, POS system, keyboards, merchandise scanners and mouse to accomplish work. Workweeks are expected to be between 36 and 40 hours with the ability to have a flexible schedule, including nights, weekends, and holidays. Regular and predictable attendance. Qualifications & Experience Must be 21 years of age or older at the time of employment. 1-2 years of retail management experience, preferably in a specialty or culinary retail environment. Proven track record of achieving sales and motivating high performing sales teams while meeting operational goals. Strong leadership skills with the ability to inspire, develop, and retain a high performing team. Excellent communication, problem-solving, and decision-making abilities. Passion for community engagement and providing exceptional customer experiences. Proficiency in Microsoft Office and retail management systems preferred.
